chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me through this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abī Ja'far عليه السلام: May a man perform the prayers of the night and all of the day with one tayammum? He said: “Yes, so long as he does not break his state of purity or come upon water.”

I said: If he finds water and hopes that he will be able to obtain other water, and thinks that he will be able to get it, but when he seeks it, that becomes difficult for him? He said: “That nullifies his tayammum, and he must repeat the tayammum.”

I said: If he finds water after having entered the salat (prayer)? He said: “Then let him turn away and perform wudu (ablution) so long as he has not bowed in ruku'. But if he has already bowed, then let him continue in his salat (prayer), for tayammum is one of the two purifications.”

key_terms.الطَّهُورَيْنِ: the two valid means of ritual purification, including tayammum and water-based purification
key_terms.تَيَمُّمٍ: dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable
key_terms.رَكَعَ: he performed ruku' (bowing) in the prayer
key_terms.مَاءً: water that restores the obligation of normal purification
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: nullifies or invalidates the prior state of purification
key_terms.يُحْدِثْ: to enter a state that nullifies ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Does one tayammum suffice for multiple prayers, and what happens if water is found during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains legal rulings concerning tayammum and its continuation across multiple prayers. It states that one tayammum remains valid until ritual nullification or the finding of water, and it clarifies what must be done if water is found before or during salat (prayer).
